items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: And Delmar Brown was another one. Delmar is a wonderful player.

ctx.x: I mean they just all think and play and perform with the same — it’s like one head. Sometimes somebody conducts, sometimes they don’t even bother. They just do it and the sax section blends so well. It’s just great. That’s the way you do a big band. Gil, it just never occurred to him. There was one European tour we did, the band was a little bigger than usual but the sax section was Dave Sanborn, Arthur Blythe, Steve Lacy and Howard Johnson and George Adams. Now these, Howard playing baritone sax — he plays it…

lot of Jimi Hendrix in Hiram’s playing. Not the exact notes or the riffs just the spirit that Hiram plays with. And Hiram does what he does and a lot of people didn’t like it. A lot of people didn’t like it. Audience. The band — we had a great time. And Hiram I remember him saying man, I don’t know what I’m doing in this band but I’m here. And Gil wrote for him, he featured him, he liked the way he played. And Delmar Brown was another one. Delmar is a wonderful player. He’s not real good at playing other people’s…
Did people in the band ever go “what is he doing?” Well I mean you just basically said it, talking about the sax players, but did you ever say like oh my God, now he’s got this guy in here.
